woodcarry.narration: The bridge stands, but the way home still refuses — block:creek.

dayLines: Travel 1 tile to forest floor.
Something moves out there — stripes resolving out of the bamboo, watching you.
This patch is worked out — step to another green patch and forage again.
The creek runs fast here — no crossing without a bridge or a swim.

Travel 1 tile to forest floor.
— Under the canopy —
Fallen trunks lie like sleeping animals, furred with moss. The ground gives underfoot — centuries of leaf-mold.
It followed you. The stripes resolving out of the bamboo is here.
Unfamiliar unknown shoots — into the bag. (Unknowns lump together; sort them at camp.)
Unfamiliar unknown nuts — into the bag. (Unknowns lump together; sort them at camp.)
Journal: Deep shade. The floor keeps its secrets.
Journal updated: a tree with lobed leaves and oval nuts in scaly caps grows here too — better than a vine with thick-skinned round fruit.
📓 Journal: you UNDERSTAND **Green Thumb, Literally**. It resonates with: something unnamed, something unnamed.

A shot in the dark — you take what's green: 4× unknown shoots, 5× unknown nuts. Into the bag, unnamed. (Not food until identified — sort them at camp.) This patch is picked clean — it'll recover in a few days.
The creek runs fast here — no crossing without a bridge or a swim.
"Nathan," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Nathan." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Nathan).
...and then it lands: A person, maybe 50s speaks 🇺🇸 English. A few shared words. Gestures. Patience.
"Faten," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Faten." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Faten).
The creek runs fast here — no crossing without a bridge or a swim.
You lash logs together. A rough bridge spans the gap. Rough wood, though — a bad storm could take it.
The tail starts lashing. This is the last warning anything ever gets.
You don't know what that was. Stripes resolving out of the bamboo, watching you. Someone at the haven should hear about this.
⚔ STRIPES RESOLVING OUT OF THE BAMBOO, WATCHING YOU! You're on your own.
Turn-based now. Tap a tile to move — speed is squares. Then act.
Not mid-fight — the barrier is the way out.
The bridge stands, but the way home still refuses — block:creek.

Travel 1 tile to forest floor.
— Under the canopy —
Leaf litter, birdcall, the smell of rot becoming soil. The woods, being the woods.
Movement — a snowshoe hare, white in winter and brown in summer, huge hind feet.
👁 Skittish — it bolts at a shadow. Come in slow, or run it down.
Some of these unknown nuts are starting to look familiar — sort them at camp in good light and the name might come to you.
Unfamiliar unknown nuts — into the bag. (Unknowns lump together; sort them at camp.)
Unfamiliar unknown berries — into the bag. (Unknowns lump together; sort them at camp.)
A sturdy stick (crafting material).
Journal: Deep shade. The floor keeps its secrets.
Journal updated: a tree with compound leaves and hard nuts grows here too — better than a tree with lobed leaves and oval nuts in scaly caps.

A shot in the dark — you take what's green: 4× unknown nuts, 4× unknown nuts, 5× unknown berries. Into the bag, unnamed. (Not food until identified — sort them at camp.) This patch is picked clean — it'll recover in a few days.
Travel 1 tile to forest floor.

Salvador leans in, voice low. "Here's what we figured out about stripes resolving out of the bamboo, watching you. Stand tall and shout. When it crouches to pounce, STAND TALL and SHOUT — bang metal, wave your arms, be loud and enormous. It expects prey to flee. Be the thing that doesn't, and the pounce dies unlaunched."

💡 COUNTER LEARNED — stripes resolving out of the bamboo, watching you: Stand tall and shout. When it crouches to pounce, STAND TALL and SHOUT — bang metal, wave your arms, be loud and enormous. It expects prey to flee. Be the thing that doesn't, and the pounce dies unlaunched. (Someone at the haven knew the trick.)

📓 Journal: Counter: Stand tall and shout — When it crouches to pounce, STAND TALL and SHOUT — bang metal, wave your arms, be loud and enormous. It expects prey to flee. Be the thing that doesn't, and the pounce dies unlaunched.
Travel 2 tiles to Haven.
You come home after 2 days. The smell of the cookfire does something to your chest you don't examine. "You're thinner," someone says. "You're still here," you say.
3 unprocessed hauls onto the counter — the clock is ticking.
Someone by the fire nods at the counter. "We pool food here. Keep what you need for the road — the rest feeds everyone, once it's food."
Nobody at the fire knows your haul any better than you do. It'll be your own hands that teach you.

You take 4 logs from the woodpile for the road home. (17 left for the hearth.)
📖 LEARNED: Old World Caches (Level 1). You know where people hid things: under floorboards, in hollow trees, behind loose bricks.
You've learned Old World Caches — it carries Eagle Eye.

Travel 2 tiles to forest floor.
— Under the canopy —
Old growth. The canopy closes overhead and the light comes down in shafts. Something rustled, and decided not to be seen.
Movement — a great horned owl, silent and huge.
👁 It waits for YOU to come close — the stillness is the trap. Spot the shape before you're in reach, and strike first. It only gets one.
You see smoke on the horizon. Emberhold — 12 people, 6 days in. fishing folk, by the look of it. They know 4 plants — 4 new to you. They've been here the whole time.
You see smoke on the horizon. Stonebridge — 11 people, 6 days in. fishing folk, by the look of it. They know 2 plants — 2 new to you. They've been here the whole time.

You catch fragments by the fire — A woman, maybe 30s, with a crooked nose telling A woman, maybe 40s, with a farmer's tan about Marisol. The truth left this story two fires ago. What's left is better theater.

Travel 2 tiles to wetland.
— Still water, cattails —
Black water under green duckweed. A turtle slides off a log with a sound like a sigh. This place has been unbothered for a long time.
Movement — a chunky brown rodent sliding along the bank, all purpose.
👁 It dives the second it spooks and stays down longer than your nerve holds. Corner it away from the water, or trap the den mouth at dusk.

Travel 1 tile to creek.
— Moving water —
The creek braids around gravel bars. Crawdads flick backward into the shadows of rocks.
Movement — crayfish under every second rock.
👁 Grab it right behind the claws, fast. It pinches.
✅ You saw the creek. Sari nods. "Good. Now we know." (+integration)

Travel 3 tiles to forest floor.
— Under the canopy —
A woodpecker works somewhere you can't see. Down here it smells of mushrooms and cold shade.

📋 Marisol wants to know what's by the creek. "Just look. Come back and tell me."
